claims.statement: The repository keeps a single canonical domain glossary in CONTEXT.md at the repo root, with the numbered decision trail in docs/adr/ beside it; each glossary entry names a canonical term together with the synonyms the glossary explicitly says to avoid.
Work in the repository is proposed and tracked as GitHub Issues operated through the gh CLI, and pull requests are explicitly not a request surface.
The repository defines exactly five canonical triage labels with default spellings: needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, and wontfix.

Contributions that name a domain concept must use the term defined in CONTEXT.md rather than a synonym the glossary avoids, and any output that contradicts an existing ADR must surface the conflict explicitly rather than silently overriding it.

The four-component vocabulary maps onto four distinct source packages: Model into src/manifold/models/, Scheduler into src/manifold/schedulers/, training Module into src/manifold/modules/, and Pipeline into src/manifold/pipelines/, with each wrapper defined in its own package.

The scale_factor is owned by the VAE wrapper: AutoencoderKL.scaling_factor is a buffer, encode returns scaled latents, decode undoes the scaling, and encode_raw returns the unscaled latent that the data stack uses to estimate 1/std(z); the training Module and inference Pipeline never reference it.
The rectified-flow transport z = t*x + (1-t)*e is owned by the Scheduler's add_noise, and the training Module calls scheduler.add_noise rather than re-deriving the noising so the two cannot drift.

The x0 Heun rollout is a single shared primitive: sample_latent_flow is called both by LatentFlowModule.sample for in-training generation and by LatentFlowPipeline.sample_latent for inference, so the train and infer paths cannot drift.

Training writes Lightning .ckpt files and the native per-component inference directory is produced by a separate export_to_native step that bakes the raw optimizer UNet weights; after the hope converter was retired this export is the sole checkpoint-to-inference path.

The callback registry is two-phase by design: resolve validates callback names and knob values at config time and fails fast, while build injects runtime objects through a typed CallbackContext, because generative callbacks need objects that do not exist at config resolution.

TrainingSpine is a composed dataclass (not a base class) that is the callback registry's single caller and owns the sequence callback-name merging, registry resolve/build, checkpoint injection, build_trainer and fit; seeding deliberately stays in each CLI shell because it must precede module construction.

Frozen arms are normal registered nn.Module children held off the optimizer and off the checkpoint by the shared FrozenArmMixin, so Lightning's automatic .to(device) owns their placement; the former object.__setattr__ unregistered-storage bypass is retired.

DevicePolicy is the single owner of the per-rank pre-process-group CUDA device, exposing pin for the one-time set_device side effect, a side-effect-free device read, and warm_device for the post-process-group VAE-warm resolution.

The FID callback enforces collective-count invariance under DDP by all_reducing a rank-local error flag with ReduceOp.MAX before any reduction-bearing phase, so a rank that fails locally makes every rank abort or proceed together instead of entering collectives in different orders.

The Reward Model is a MONAI PatchDiscriminator behind a mean-pooling head that emits a raw patch-logit mean with no sigmoid, owns no generation rollout, and scores the terminal latent unconditionally for both GRPO policies.

The Reward Module holds the frozen JiT x0-denoiser as a registered, dual-excluded arm and rolls fresh preference pairs inside each fit step, drawing both flow-times from U[0,1) and labelling the larger-t half the winner and the smaller-t half the loser by input corruption level, so the winner and loser corruption ranges overlap.

The GRPO singular-branching rollout runs one deterministic Heun anchor per group, branches exactly one stochastic SDE step off the anchor at each perturbed step, then rolls a deterministic Heun suffix to the terminal latent the frozen reward scores; the whole rollout is no_grad so only the single perturbed step holds a graph.

The GRPO transition policy's Gaussian kernel is owned by the scheduler (FlowMatchGRPOScheduler.sde_step_mean returns the mean and std), while the transition log-density and the group-normalized advantage live in the module, keeping the policy's parameters separate from the policy itself.

GRPOModule infers which policy it trains from whether a ControlNet is present rather than from a numbered mode: with a ControlNet the base UNet is frozen and dual-excluded and only the ControlNet is optimized, otherwise the JiT UNet is the policy, and both score z_K with the same unconditional reward.

The ControlNet is a trainable clone of the base UNet encoder plus zero-initialized zero-conv layers whose residuals enter the frozen base through MONAI's native down_block_additional_residuals and mid_block_additional_residual forward arguments, using an out-of-place base forward so gradients can flow back from the base output into the ControlNet.

The ControlNet's direction head is a learned MLP over concat(embed(src), embed(tgt+offset)) on the ControlNet class-embedding path, with the optional paired_direction_offset shifting the target label row to break A-to-B symmetry, replacing the retired summed-label base-UNet mechanism.

Paired fidelity is MONAI 3D PSNR and SSIM computed on VAE-decoded, per-sample min-max-normalized volumes with data_range 1.0, and the same metric helper backs both the offline before/after comparison and the observe-only in-training monitor that logs val/psnr and val/ssim without touching checkpoint selection or the loss.

There are two configuration systems by design: the OmegaConf experiment config composes env, recipe and network-construction kwargs with _base_ inheritance, ??? fail-fast paths and CLI/dotlist overrides and never persists the components it builds, while the JSON component config is written by register_to_config/ConfigMixin and round-tripped by from_pretrained/save_pretrained.

The ADR trail in docs/adr/ records 37 numbered decisions, many carrying explicit supersession banners that mark a decision as retired history rather than current policy (for example ADR-0013, ADR-0018, ADR-0024 and ADR-0016).

CONTEXT.md's "Training callbacks & device ownership (ADR-0029-0033, pending)" marker is stale: the callback registry, the FID helper split with collective-count hardening, the frozen-arm registration, the TrainingSpine and the scripts/ removal are all implemented, and the two follow-ons that completed the refactor (DevicePolicy and the in-training paired-fidelity monitor) ship as well.

CONTEXT.md's description of the frozen JiT denoiser and the frozen Reward Model as "unregistered" is stale: both are now registered nn.Module children held off the optimizer and off the checkpoint by FrozenArmMixin, and a stale echo of the old wording survives in a source comment.

ADR front-matter status banners are not a reliable implementation signal: ADR-0017 still declares status "proposed" and says the implementation is not landed, yet the latent warm now runs inside LatentWarmDataModule.setup() after the process group exists.

The superseded vocabulary has no live implementation: the paired reward module and CLI, the Brownian-bridge GRPO scheduler, the paired singular-branch rollout and the hope-to-native converter are all absent from src/, and no GRPO mode flag exists in the source tree.

The scripts/ directory was eliminated: export_checkpoint.py was migrated into the manifold-export entry point in src/manifold/training/export_cli.py, the offline pair-generation script was retired, and pyproject.toml is the single source of truth for the console scripts.

docs/prd/ddp-correctness.md is a proposed plan rather than a decision record: its locked choice to keep validation rank-0-only was later reversed by ADR-0025, and it cites modules that no longer exist such as paired_cli.py and psnr_ssim_callback.py.

The historical paired console entry points no longer exist in pyproject.toml, and the surviving manifold-export pipeline choices are jit and controlnet; the paired choice string remains in export_cli.py as a stale reference to a deleted module.
